Existing backend effect IDs are parent references; duplicate child IDs never dispatch again, and bind retries cannot reopen closed admission. SandboxClient sends a distinct stable child operation ID per HTTP request under the existing compound effect. Matching remote operation/journal receipts append to ExternalEffectEvidence under the exact live effect claim without prematurely completing the parent; mismatched/incomplete receipts fail closed. Late evidence can be retained after Agent/resource close, but stale or expired effect workers cannot append it.

An actual SQL Driver/Effect -> SandboxClient -> Action Server -> local subprocess test leaves backend admission open, closes only the remote gate, and proves the second command never starts. Opt-in unprivileged_child_v1 executes shell, SSE shell, PTY, stdio MCP, relay and install scripts through a fresh isolated Python worker. A real startup probe and every child enforce Linux NoNewPrivs, empty supplementary groups, permanent non-root UID/GID and zero inheritable/permitted/effective/ambient capabilities. Invalid users, unsupported kernels or failed transitions never fall back to root.

Target loader and Python environment variables are serialized outside argv and installed only after privilege drop; service control/provider credentials are filtered. Configured PTYs attach their controlling terminal in the fresh worker instead of running Python after fork in a threaded server; disconnect cleanup reaps the owned shell before cancellation can interrupt it. Docker/bootstrap/narrow deploy package and syntax-check the helper; isolation is not enabled by default because MCP config/backup/diagnostic paths, journal path ancestry and existing-volume ownership remain unresolved.

Opt-in unprivileged_files_v1 routes upload, download, list/read/write, glob/grep and skill CRUD/install/archive/export HTTP handlers through a one-request ordinary-user worker over anonymous pipes. The parent performs authentication and persistent resource admission, rechecks immediately before spawn, strips service/auth/resource headers, forwards bounded frames with backpressure and has no privileged fallback. Existing handlers run after the permanent identity transition; the worker opens no listener and holds no supervisor credential.

Skill directory initialization and the skill portion of catalogue/version projections use the same isolated worker. Parent boot identity and MCP projection remain stable across worker restarts. Worker setup failures, incomplete frames and cancellation do not fall back to root; cancellation kills/reaps the owned worker while remote outcomes conservatively remain unknown. Upload filenames cannot escape the destination through path separators, permission errors return 403, inaccessible links no longer break file listings and UTF-8 download names use encoded response headers.
